name: Hassan
headline: Child marriages doubled in two years and put Hassan at the top of the state.
summary: Reporting says child marriages in Hassan doubled over two years, placing the district first in the state, with poverty and single-parent households behind withdrawals. A survey found 1,819 out-of-school children, concentrated in particular taluks, and police formed an all-women squad, Hasanamba Pade, to track dropouts and stop underage marriages.

reasons.detail: Child marriages in the district doubled over two years, the highest in the state at the time of the report.
Minor girls are reported to be taken and married under the guise of love affairs, complicating efforts to return them to class.
A survey identified 1,819 out-of-school children, concentrated in specific taluks.

reasons.factor: Girls leaving high school, child marriage
reasons.detail: The Deputy Commissioner urged tracking of girl students dropping out of high school and monitoring of mass marriages to curb child marriage, reflecting official concern that girls exit through early marriage.
Thirty-two government primary schools were closed, 11 in Belur and 10 in Hassan taluk among them, reducing nearby schooling; link to secondary dropout is inferred, not stated.
The same review asked officials to look into rising missing-person cases of women and girls and run awareness programmes for girls.
